Name: Hallows_Eve_Gravekeeper
$Comment: The Gravekeeper's conversation, what pressing F on him opens in the Forgotten Temple. He stands there
while Hallow's Eve runs and on a full moon outside it (his placement's Season,
Seasons_Of_Orbis_Gravekeeper_Nights), and this one conversation serves both: each night's lines show
while that night is live, read through ziggfreedcommon:calendar_live, Hallows_Eve or
Seasons_Of_Orbis_Restless_Moon. The two are never live at once (the Restless Moon is a full moon while
Hallow's Eve is not running), so a visit only ever sees one night's lines. He is one of the Hallowed and
keeps the graveyards for them, so his own lines name neither Old Jack nor Hallow's Eve as his reason to
be there: Jack comes up only as the man who sells the candles his gate burns, and on the ember line,
shown to a player on Old Jack's errand, as the one who sent them. He never contracts: I am, it is, does
not. That keeps him apart from Old Jack, who always does.
HOW A SCREEN IS PICKED. First is walked top to bottom, then Fallback. On a full moon he opens on
restless: the dead are restless under the full moon, putting down skeletons and zombies while it is up
earns favor with the Hallowed (the Undead row in Reputations/HallowsEvePack/Hallows_Eve_Hallowed.json),
and the graveyard behind him will not stay quiet: what it costs to go in and what waits there. It
comes first, so nothing of Hallow's Eve opens on a full moon and the hard ride's introduction waits for
Hallow's Eve. During Hallow's Eve the ember line comes first, while the player carries Old Jack's hard
step (hallows_eve_old_jack_horseman_hard): it says the ember only drops on the hard ride. Then the hard
ride's introduction, once per character (OnceId hard_open), for a player who has finished The Rider
(hallows_eve_old_jack_horseman). Every other visit opens on menu.
THE LINES. gk_menu is on every screen a visit opens on, each way in shown only on its own night. During
Hallow's Eve: take me in (the Horseman's graveyard) and take me on the hard ride (the hard graveyard,
shown only to a player who has finished The Rider; this condition is the hard graveyard's only quest
gate, since the dungeon itself asks only for its season and its candle, so no other line or press-F may
open it). On a full moon: lay the restless dead to rest (the restless graveyard, an endless run of the
dead with the Voidtaken Horseman every fifth wave). On both: who he is, and goodnight. Each way in is
the Dungeon destination, which sends the player in with their party, or says why it refused. The who
screen carries gk_back: back to the night's opening screen (menu or restless, each on its own night),
or goodnight. To add a line for one night, gate it the same way. The trick-or-treat line is not here:
the DialogueExtensions file Hallows_Eve_Trick_Or_Treat adds it to every conversation during Hallow's
Eve, this one included, and its favor goes to the Hallowed, his own people. Harvest Feast's
invitation line leaves this conversation out by name, since he never comes to the feast.
THE PRICE. Each graveyard's EntryCost (ZiggfreedCommon/Dungeons) takes its price from whoever opens an
area for their party: a Grave Candle for the Horseman's graveyard, a Burning Grave Candle for the hard
ride, five bone fragments for the restless graveyard, and an Eternal Candle opens the Horseman's and
the restless one without being spent. The menu line says the gate wants a Grave Candle, the hard
ride's introduction and the ember line name the Burning one, each saying Old Jack sells it, and the
restless line names the fragments; each way-in label shows its price. Option labels take no number
from the file, so a changed count is written into the label and its screen's text in every language.
Picking a way in opens CommonLib's confirm screen in this page's place (the dungeon's
EntryCost.Confirm, built like the game's portal summon screen): the graveyard's name and description,
the price, how many the player holds and how many it takes, and the button that pays and sends the
party in. With too few, the button is off and nothing is spent. A partymate following into a
graveyard their party already holds skips the screen and walks in free.
